h: Tamar Valley adventures beyond the mine
p: Morwellham sits in one of the most beautiful river valleys in the South West, and it's worth taking time to explore the wider area. The Tamar forms the border between Devon and Cornwall, and its wooded banks, old quays and mining chimneys give the valley a unique character. Walking trails from the quay take you up into the woods and along the river, and on a sunny day the views are gorgeous.

Across the water in Cornwall, Cotehele is a Tudor house and estate run by the National Trust, with its own little quay and gardens running down to the river. A little further downstream, the village of Calstock is dominated by its tall railway viaduct, which carries the Tamar Valley Line across the river and makes for a stunning photograph.

Tavistock is a lovely market town and a great base for the area. It's known for its pannier market, a covered market selling everything from crafts to antiques, and the remains of the old abbey are scattered through the town centre. The statue of Sir Francis Drake, who was born nearby, is another local landmark. Dartmoor starts right on the doorstep, and the little church on top of Brent Tor is a striking sight on its volcanic hill.

Back at Morwellham, give yourself plenty of time. The mine ride, the village and the riverside walks add up to a full day, so arriving early and pacing yourself will help everyone enjoy the whole lot. Wellies or sturdy shoes are a good idea for the trails.
